prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Thực đơn quán phở (language vi).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Món" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 106px
  col 2: header "Giá" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 3: header "Thành phần" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 1507px
  col 4: header "Ghi chú" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 419px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Help diners choose a phở dish by comparing its price, ingredients and any accompanying notes.","reading":"Readers scan dish names down the first column, compare prices, then read ingredients and notes across the chosen row. The long ingredient descriptions will largely determine row height, leaving room for notes to wrap alongside them.","groups":["Món and Giá form the compact identification and price pair used for quick comparison.","Thành phần and Ghi chú are descriptive columns read alongside each dish; both can use multiple lines, but ingredients need more space."],"keep_intact":["Dish names and prices should fit on one line for easy scanning.","Individual words, currency amounts and identifiers should not be broken."],"may_wrap":["Ingredient descriptions can wrap naturally at spaces and punctuation.","Notes can wrap naturally, often within height already needed by the ingredients."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [127, 80, 360, 152] · table 720×673px · row heights [36, 129, 83, 106, 83, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [127, 80, 300, 212] · table 720×813px · row heights [36, 153, 106, 129, 106, 129, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [127, 80, 420, 92] · table 720×999px · row heights [36, 176, 153, 129, 153, 176, 176] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
